riesz_displacement_series — QUAT motion op

• Data kinds: video → pairs

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.riesz_displacement_series(video, f_lo, f_hi, fps, scales: 'int' = 4) -> 'np.ndarray' (implementation को सीधे call करना हो तो import quatimage; quatimage.riesz_displacement_series(video, f_lo, f_hi, fps, scales: 'int' = 4) -> 'np.ndarray', registry से लेना हो तो opsquat.get("riesz_displacement_series"))

उपयोग

monogenic phase से पूरे frame का displacement waveform। → (T, 2)।

> नीचे का विस्तृत विवरण मूल text में है — सारांश और headings का अनुवाद हो चुका है।

The contrast-weighted spatial mean of riesz_displacement: the rigid-body motion of the scene in pixels, one (dx, dy) row per frame. The (n, 2) layout is the shared 1-D convention (dsp.spectrum, funct1d, opsoptics's MTF curves), so the trace can be handed to dsp.spectrum to read off a resonant frequency without any repacking.

Weights are the |z|^2 contrast the field solve uses, restricted to the pixels marked valid, so blank regions do not drag the average towards zero. A clip with no valid pixel anywhere (a constant image) returns exact zeros rather than dividing by zero.

Accuracy, the J0 cliff and the multi-orientation failure all inherit from riesz_displacement — read its head-to-head table before trusting a number from here. On a single-grating 64x64x64 / 8 px / 4 Hz clip a true 0.5 px amplitude is recovered as 0.50000000000000 px (2.2e-16 relative); on the two-grating motionmag.synthesize_translation default the same 0.5 px comes back 13.0 % low, with nothing to signal it.
